sentences.speech: Build a complete Space Invaders game in Scratch 3.
This self-guided advanced-beginner course is for ages 10-14 with about one year of Scratch experience.
You will create an alien fleet that moves together, two reusable shots, bunkers that show damage, a bonus Mothership, scoring, and clear ways to win and lose.
Use coordinates, loops, conditions, variables, messages, and clones in Scratch 3.
Create 24 Alien clones in an 8 by 3 grid and move them as one fleet.
Control game phases and messages with scripts on the Stage.
Build reusable Player Laser and Enemy Shot sprites without cloning either shot.
Give Bunker clones independent health and costume damage.
Finish a game with scoring, a bonus Mothership, and reliable win and loss rules.
You have used Scratch for about one year and can create a blank Scratch 3 project.
You can connect scripts, choose values from block menus, rename sprites, and use basic loops and conditions.
You do not need to have built a full game or used clones before.
Use Scratch online at scratch.mit.edu, signed in to your Scratch account.
You will not download or upload project files.
Complete all six chapters in order; this course has one required path.
Plan for 90-120 minutes per chapter.
Scratch saves your project to your account; also choose File > Save now at each chapter checkpoint.
To continue later, sign in, open My Stuff, and click See inside on your project.
Use the exact sprite, variable, costume, backdrop, and message names shown so the code references match.
Keep every costume centered and inside the maximum width and height given in Chapter 1 so sprites do not overlap by accident.
Use the green flag as the only way to start or restart the game.
pixel
One of the tiny dots that make up the screen.
The Stage is 480 pixels wide and 360 pixels high.
coordinate
A number that says where a sprite is.
x goes from -240 on the left to 240 on the right.
y goes from -180 at the bottom to 180 at the top.
The middle of the Stage is x 0, y 0.
clone
A temporary copy of a sprite that runs the clone scripts and keeps its own sprite-only variable values.
shared variable
A shared variable made with For all sprites.
The Stage and every sprite can read or change it.
sprite-only variable
A variable made with For this sprite only.
Each clone gets its own value for that variable.
message
A named broadcast that starts matching when I receive scripts.
state
A stored value such as starting, playing, won, or lost that describes what the game may do now.
reusable sprite
One sprite that is hidden, moved, and used again instead of creating clones.
Active variable
A 0-or-1 variable that shows whether a reusable sprite is busy.
Checking it prevents the same action from happening twice.
lane
One vertical firing column in the eight-column alien fleet.
A reliable game starts with a clear plan.
The Stage will reset shared data and control the alien march.
One Alien sprite will make 24 clones.
Player Laser, Enemy Shot, and Mothership will each be one reusable sprite with no clones.
Each of the three Bunker clones will remember its own Health value.
Sign in to Scratch and click Create.
Keep the Cat for now, because you will use it in the next step.
Type Space Invaders in the project title box at the top of the editor.
On paper or in a note, write down the six sprites you will need: Player, Alien, Player Laser, Enemy Shot, Bunker, and Mothership.
Picture an 8-column by 3-row alien fleet.
That is 24 aliens.
Aliens Left counts up to 24 during setup, and the player wins when it reaches 0.
Think through the two ways to lose: an Enemy Shot touches Player, or an Alien reaches the invasion line.
That is a low line you will draw on the backdrop in the next step.
Remember the restart rule: after a win or loss, click the green flag.
Do not build a Restart button or an in-game restart message.
One reusable sprite works well when only one laser or shot of that type may be active.
One message tells every Alien clone to update for the same fleet step.
The plan includes many laser or shot clones.
Cross out plans to clone either shot.
Player Laser and Enemy Shot will hide, move, and be reused.
Keep clones only for Alien and Bunker.
Explain the plan for your sprites without looking back at the lesson.
You can name all six sprites, the two sprite types that use clones, the two reusable shots that do not use clones, and both ways to lose.
You identify Alien and Bunker as the only cloned sprites.
You identify the green flag as the only restart.
You explain that Aliens Left reaching zero causes the win.
Scratch uses numbers to say where a sprite is.
These numbers count pixels, the tiny dots that make up the screen.
The Stage is 480 pixels wide and 360 pixels high.
A costume that is 36 pixels wide is small: about 13 of them fit side by side across the Stage.
Try the numbers with the Cat now, because every later step uses them.
Drag the Cat around the Stage and watch the x and y boxes under the Stage change.
Use those boxes to move the Cat to x 0, y 0.
The Cat jumps to the middle of the Stage.
Drag the Cat right, then left.
x gets bigger going right.
Left of the middle, x has a minus sign.
Drag the Cat up, then down.
y gets bigger going up.
Below the middle, y has a minus sign.
Use the y box to move the Cat to y negative 60, then to y negative 120.
The bigger the number after the minus sign, the lower the Cat goes.
Drag a change x by 10 block into the Code area and click it a few times.
x changes by 10 on each click, so the Cat moves 10 pixels to the right.
Change the block to change y by negative 10 and click it a few times.
The Cat moves down 10 pixels on each click.
Delete that block, then delete the Cat by clicking the trash can on its thumbnail in the sprite list.
The edges of the Stage are x negative 240 on the left, x 240 on the right, y negative 180 at the bottom, and y 180 at the top.
Press Enter after you type in a box.
The Cat does not move when you type a number.
Press Enter after typing.
Make sure the Cat is selected in the sprite list.
Without looking back, say where each of these is: x 0, y 0; x negative 210; and y negative 150.
Then say what change y by negative 10 does.
x 0, y 0 is the middle of the Stage.
x negative 210 is near the left edge.
y negative 150 is near the bottom.
change y by negative 10 moves a sprite down 10 pixels.
You can explain what a minus sign means for x and for y.
You know that a bigger x means further right and a bigger y means higher up.
The Cat is deleted.
Names matter because Scratch places sprite names inside sensing and motion blocks.
Set up every game object now so later instructions can use exact names.
Click the Stage in the bottom right of the editor, then click the Backdrops tab.
Make a dark background in one of two ways.
Either fill the blank backdrop with a dark color, or choose a dark space backdrop from the library and then delete the blank one.
Rename the dark backdrop Space.
Right-click the Space thumbnail and choose duplicate.
Do this twice, then name the two copies You Win and Game Over.
You should now have exactly three backdrops.
On You Win, use the Text tool and a light color to type the words You Win in large letters.
On Game Over, do the same with the words Game Over.
Select Space again.
The next three instructions tell you what to type on it with the Text tool.
Use a light color so the words show up.
This is only information for the player, so no code is needed yet.
Type the controls: Arrow keys: move.
Space key: fire.
Green flag: start or restart.
Type the goal: Destroy all Aliens to win.
Avoid Enemy Shots.
Stop the Aliens from reaching the invasion line.
Type the scoring: Aliens: 10 points each.
Mothership: 50 points.
The Mothership is a bonus enemy ship you will build in Chapter 5.
Keep the words small so they do not distract from the game.
Sprites move in front of the backdrop, so the words cannot affect play.
To make each sprite below, point at the cat button in the bottom right and click Paint.
Rename the sprite in the Sprite box under the Stage.
Paint each shape over the small center mark in the middle of the canvas.
A costume is centered when that mark is in the middle of the artwork.
Set the Outline number to 0 so an outline does not add to the size.
Create a ship sprite named Player.
Center its artwork and keep its visible costume no larger than 36 pixels wide by 18 pixels high.
Select Player and use the y box under the Stage to move it to y negative 60.
Player now marks the height of the invasion line.
A later script moves it back to its real starting place.
Select the Stage and the Space backdrop.
Use the Line tool and a dim color to draw a thin line across the whole backdrop.
Watch the Stage preview and make the line pass through the middle of Player.
Use the Text tool to label the line invasion line.
An alien that drops below this line ends the game.
Create an enemy sprite named Alien.
Center its artwork and keep its visible costume no larger than 32 pixels wide by 18 pixels high.
Paint two thin, upright sprites named Player Laser and Enemy Shot.
Center each one and keep it no larger than 4 pixels wide by 10 pixels high.
Make Player Laser bright and Enemy Shot red.
Create a centered Bunker no larger than 56 pixels wide by 18 pixels high.
Create a centered Mothership no larger than 40 pixels wide by 12 pixels high.
Check each sprite on its Costumes tab.
The thumbnail shows two numbers, such as 36 x 18.
The first is the width and the second is the height.
If a shape is too big, select it with the arrow tool and drag a corner to shrink it.
Do not use the Size box under the Stage, because that does not change the costume's numbers.
Do not continue until every costume is centered and inside its maximum size.
Simple geometric art is easier to resize and test than detailed art.
Use the zoom buttons below the paint canvas to draw tiny costumes more easily.
A 4-pixel laser is only as wide as four of those tiny dots.
A later block menu does not show the expected sprite.
Check spelling and spaces in every sprite name.
Make sure Player Laser and Enemy Shot are two different sprites.
Check the sprite list and the Stage's backdrop list.
The project has exactly the six required named sprites, three named backdrops, centered costumes within the size limits, and visible player instructions on the Space backdrop.
All sprite names match the lesson exactly.
Only the Space, You Win, and Game Over backdrops exist.
The Space backdrop shows the controls, goal, dangers, and scoring while every sprite costume is centered and inside its maximum box.
The Stage and sprites need the same names for game information.
Variables made For all sprites store shared facts and fleet coordinates.
Variables made For this sprite only let each Alien clone remember its own row and column and each Bunker clone remember its own health.
Make these variables with For all sprites: Score, Aliens Left, Game State, Stage, Fleet X, Fleet Y, Laser Active, Enemy Shot Active, and Shot Lane.
The variable named Stage only shares its name with Scratch's Stage.
It stores the number of the fleet's movement phase.
On the Alien sprite, make My Column, My Row, and Is Clone with For this sprite only.
On the Bunker sprite, make Health and Bunker Number with For this sprite only.
On the Mothership sprite, make Active with For this sprite only.
On the Stage, drag out a temporary broadcast block.
Open its message menu, choose New message, and create Reset Game and Start Game.
Later chapters create each new message when its first real script is built.
Leave the temporary block in the Code area for now.
You will delete it in the next step, once the startup script uses both messages.
Hide every variable display except Score and Aliens Left.
To hide one, untick the checkbox beside its name in the Variables list.
The choice For this sprite only appears while making a variable.
Capitalization must match because the finished code uses these exact names.
Every Bunker clone later loses health together.
Delete and remake Health as For this sprite only on Bunker.
Do the same for Bunker Number.
Alien identities do not stay independent.
Confirm My Column, My Row, and Is Clone are Alien variables made with For this sprite only.
Sort the variables into For all sprites and For this sprite only groups.

Nine For all sprites variables, three Alien For this sprite only variables, two Bunker For this sprite only variables, one Mothership For this sprite only variable, and the two Chapter 1 messages exist.
Only Score and Aliens Left are visible on the Stage.
Reset Game and Start Game appear in a broadcast menu.
Each For this sprite only variable was created on the correct sprite.
One script on the Stage is the only way the game starts.
It resets shared values, tells every sprite to prepare, and starts play only after preparation finishes.
Player checks the arrow keys in its own movement loop and keeps its x coordinate inside the Stage.
A later chapter adds a separate firing loop, so waiting for the Space key to be released never pauses movement.
On the Stage, add the green-flag script.
Every block is in the finished code section on this page.
If that section is closed, click Show finished code.
Use broadcast Reset Game and wait so all setup finishes before Game State becomes playing.
Delete the temporary broadcast block from the last step.
The startup script now uses both messages, so Scratch keeps them.
On Player, reset its position to x 0, y negative 150, which is near the bottom of the Stage, and show it when Reset Game arrives.
On Alien, Player Laser, Enemy Shot, Bunker, and Mothership, add a when I receive Reset Game script with hide.
In later chapters, add each sprite's other reset blocks to this same script.
On Player, start a movement script when Start Game arrives.
Add repeat until, and for its condition put Game State equals playing inside a not block.
Movement then stops when the game ends.
Move left or right by 6 while the matching arrow key is pressed.
Player moves 6 pixels each time the loop runs, so a bigger number would make it faster.
Keep Player between x negative 210 and x 210.
The edges of the Stage are at x negative 240 and x 240, so Player stays fully on the Stage.
Click the green flag and move to both sides.
With Player selected, the x box under the Stage should stop at -210 and 210.
Put the two edge checks inside the movement loop, after the movement blocks.
The Stage uses broadcast Reset Game and wait, so it does not send Start Game until every when I receive Reset Game script has finished.
Player moves once and stops.
Put all key and edge checks inside the repeat until Game State is not playing loop.
Use sensing blocks key left arrow pressed and key right arrow pressed.
Old values remain after another play.
Make sure all reset blocks are directly under the Stage green-flag event.
Restart only with the green flag.
Start twice and move Player against both side boundaries.
Each green-flag click shows the Space backdrop, resets all shared values, and places a controllable Player at the bottom.
Score and Aliens Left both display 0 for now.
Game State becomes playing after reset.
Every non-Player sprite is hidden during setup.
Player never moves past x negative 210 or x 210.
This checkpoint prevents problems in later chapters.
The green flag must be the only reset, and all names must be exact before you add clones and shots.
Choose File > Save now.
Click My Stuff at the top of the page, then click See inside on Space Invaders.
Open a broadcast menu and check that it shows Reset Game and Start Game but no unused message1.
Click the green flag, move Player, then click the green flag again while Player is moving.
With Player selected, check that the boxes under the Stage show x 0, y negative 150, and that the Space backdrop returns.
Compare your Stage and Player scripts with the complete Chapter 1 code in the finished code section on this page.
Do not continue until every required sprite, variable, message, and backdrop name matches.
Click a variable block in the blocks list to check its current value without leaving its visible display turned on.
A second green-flag click safely stops old scripts before starting fresh ones.
Some sprite appears before the game starts.
Confirm Alien, Player Laser, Enemy Shot, Bunker, and Mothership each receive Reset Game and hide.
Do not rely on manually hiding a sprite in the editor; the reset scripts must create the clean setup.
Pass the Chapter 1 launch test.
The project always reaches the same clean starting state, and Player cannot move past either edge.
Two green-flag starts produce identical values and positions.
There is no Restart sprite, message, key, or button.
The project has been saved after the test.
The hidden original Alien creates all the clones.
Before it creates each clone, it changes its own row and column values.
Scratch copies those For this sprite only values into the new clone, so every Alien clone remembers its row and column.
Select Alien and confirm My Column, My Row, and Is Clone say For this sprite only.
On Alien's Costumes tab, check that the centered costume is no larger than 32 x 18.
Those are the width and height in pixels, and they stop rows and columns from overlapping.
Find Alien's existing when I receive Reset Game script from Chapter 1.
Under its hide block, add the cloning blocks from the finished code section on this page.
Do not add a second when I receive Reset Game event block.
Set Is Clone to 1 before creating clones and back to 0 afterward.
This tells the hidden original apart from its clones.
Change Aliens Left by 1 for each clone so the final count is exactly 24.
The inner loop makes eight columns; the outer loop makes three rows.
A clone receives copies of the original's For this sprite only values when create clone of myself runs.
Aliens Left ends at 8 or 3.
Put change Aliens Left by 1 inside the inner repeat 8 loop.
Make sure the repeat 8 loop is inside repeat 3.
Run the cloning script and check Aliens Left.
The original Alien stays hidden and Aliens Left reaches exactly 24.
The outer repeat 3 makes three rows, and its inner repeat 8 creates eight clones in each row.
The original ends with Is Clone set to 0.
Aliens Left displays 24 after reset.
Every clone works out its position from the fleet's starting coordinates and its own row and column.
Columns are 45 pixels apart and rows are 35 pixels apart.
An Alien is at most 32 pixels wide and 18 pixels high, so there is always a gap between them.
The same formula keeps working when the Stage changes Fleet X and Fleet Y.
Under when I start as a clone, add the Motion block go to x: y:.
For x, build Fleet X plus My Column times 45.
For y, build Fleet Y minus My Row times 35.
Show the clone after both coordinates are set.
Click the green flag and count eight aliens in each of three rows.
If aliens overlap, make the Alien costume smaller.
Do not change the 45 and 35 spacing numbers.
Build the multiplication operator first.
Then place it inside the addition or subtraction operator.
Row zero is at Fleet Y, which starts at 130, near the top of the Stage.
Rows one and two are lower.
All 24 aliens pile onto one position.
Confirm the row and column variables were made For this sprite only on Alien.
Check that the hidden original changes My Column after every clone and My Row after every row.
The grid slopes diagonally instead of forming rows.
Reset My Column to 0 at the start of each outer-loop pass.
Count the aliens and check the fleet's shape.
Exactly 24 visible Alien clones form eight straight columns and three straight rows near the top.
Leftmost and rightmost aliens remain on the Stage.
Rows and columns have even spacing.
The hidden original Alien is not visible.
Only the Stage changes Fleet X and Fleet Y.
It then broadcasts one of three march messages.
Each live clone uses the same formula to work out its new position.
This keeps the rows and columns evenly spaced after other clones are destroyed.
Add a when I receive script to Alien.
Choose New message and name it March Right.
Add an if Is Clone equals 1 check so only clones respond.
Inside that check, use the same x and y position formula as clone placement.
Duplicate that script for March Left.
In the event block's message menu, choose New message and create that exact name.
Duplicate the script again.
Choose New message and create March Down.
After go to x y, add an if that checks y position less than negative 60 and Game State equals playing.
y negative 60 is the height of your invasion line, so y position less than negative 60 means the Alien is lower than the line.
Inside that if, set Game State to lost.
Then choose New message in the broadcast block, create Lose, and broadcast it.
Do not change fleet coordinates in Alien.
Only the Stage changes Fleet X and Fleet Y.
Keep the Is Clone equals 1 check so the hidden original does not act like a fleet member.
To test, click the green flag so the clones exist.
Then on the Stage, drag out one temporary broadcast and wait block for each march message.
Drag out a temporary change Fleet X by 10 block and click it.
Then click a broadcast and wait block.
Every Alien should take a small jump to the right, and the gaps between them should stay the same.
Try each message, also changing Fleet Y to test March Down.
Delete all of the temporary test blocks from the Stage.
All three when I receive scripts use the same coordinate formula.
Only March Down adds the invasion check.
The message name describes what the Stage changed, not a separate movement rule inside Alien.
Aliens spread apart or move at different speeds.
Use go to x y, not change x or change y, in all three when I receive scripts.
Compare all three formulas character by character.
Think back over your march-message tests, then check the Stage for leftover test blocks.
Every Alien moves to the position given by Fleet X, Fleet Y, and its own row and column.
All three messages have matching when I receive scripts.
Each when I receive script checks Is Clone equals 1.
No Alien when I receive script changes Fleet X or Fleet Y.
The temporary test scripts on the Stage have been deleted.
The Stage controls the fleet with scripts that finish each phase instead of letting 24 clones choose their own movement.
Each move changes the fleet's position by 10 pixels.
In phase 1, the fleet moves right five times.
In phase 2, it moves left nine times.
In phase 3, it moves right nine times.
Each side-to-side phase ends with one move down.
The Stage variable then switches between 2 and 3.
On the Stage, start a new script with when I receive Start Game.
These steps build the march script in the finished code section on this page.
Add repeat until.
For its condition, put Game State equals playing inside a not block.
Inside the repeat, add an if then else that checks Stage equals 1.
Inside its else, add a second if then else that checks Stage equals 2.
The three open spaces will hold phase 1, phase 2, and phase 3.
As you build each phase below, put the blocks of every sideways move inside their own if Game State equals playing.
Do the same for every down move.
This makes the fleet stop as soon as the game ends.
In the Stage equals 1 space, build phase 1.
Repeat five times: add 10 to Fleet X, use broadcast March Right and wait, and then wait 0.35 seconds.
After phase 1, subtract 10 from Fleet Y, use broadcast March Down and wait, and set the Stage variable to 2.
In the Stage equals 2 space, build phase 2 with nine left moves and one down move.
Then set the Stage variable to 3.
In the last else space, build phase 3 with nine right moves and one down move.
Then set the Stage variable to 2.
Check that every coordinate change and march broadcast is on the Stage, not on Alien.
Broadcast and wait lets all clones finish positioning before the next fleet step.
The fleet starts in the center.
Phase 1 moves it five steps to the right edge.
The nine-step phases then travel the full width from edge to edge.
The fleet races down immediately.
Put the 0.35-second wait inside each horizontal repeat.
Put each downward move after, not inside, the horizontal repeat.
The fleet keeps moving in one direction.
Phase 2 must set the Stage variable to 3, and phase 3 must set the Stage variable to 2.
Phase 2 changes Fleet X by -10; phase 3 changes it by 10.
Watch at least three complete horizontal phases.
All 24 aliens move as one shape, step down only at an edge, and set Game State to lost once an alien drops below the invasion line.
The spaces between aliens never change size while the fleet moves.
Only scripts on the Stage change Fleet X, Fleet Y, and the Stage variable.
A low alien sets Game State to lost and broadcasts Lose.
Only the Stage changes the shared fleet coordinates.
Each movement phase finishes before the next one starts, and every clone uses its own row and column to find the correct place.
Choose File > Save now.
Start the game and check that Aliens Left reaches 24 before movement starts.
Count eight aliens across and three down.
Watch the phase 1, phase 2, and phase 3 sequence.
Turn on the Game State variable display and let the fleet descend without shooting it.
When an alien drops below the invasion line, the fleet stops and Game State becomes lost.
Chapter 5 adds the Game Over screen.
Turn the display off again.
Temporarily show the Stage, Fleet X, and Fleet Y variable displays while testing, then hide them.
The project may continue visibly after Lose until Chapter 5 adds the matching when I receive Lose script.
An invasion is reported too early.
Keep the y check only in the clone's when I receive March Down script.
Confirm that script checks Is Clone equals 1; the hidden original must not check invasion.
Pass the fleet count, shape, movement, and invasion tests.
Twenty-four clones remember their rows and columns and move together under the Stage's control.
The count is exactly 24 after every green-flag restart.
Only the three march messages controlled by the Stage move the fleet.
An alien below the invasion line changes Game State to lost.
Player Laser is one reusable sprite and does not create clones.
Laser Active is 0 while the laser is ready and hidden, then 1 while it is flying.
Checking this variable prevents a second shot from moving the sprite before the first shot ends.
Player firing runs separately from Player movement, so waiting for the Space key to be released cannot block the arrow keys.
Select Player Laser and remove any clone blocks if you experimented earlier.
Find Player Laser's existing when I receive Reset Game script from Chapter 1.
Snap set Laser Active to 0 directly under its hide block.
On Player Laser's Costumes tab, check that it is centered and no larger than 4 x 10.
A 10-pixel laser that moves 10 pixels at a time cannot jump over an 18-pixel alien, and it cannot touch two rows at once.
On Player, add a second, separate when I receive Start Game script for firing.
Use the same repeat until not Game State equals playing loop.
Do not put firing inside the movement script.
Inside the firing loop, add a condition that checks whether the Space key is pressed and Laser Active is 0.
Inside that condition, set Laser Active to 1 first so the next loop pass sees that a shot has started.
Choose New message in a broadcast block, create Fire Laser, and broadcast it.
Wait until the Space key is released or Game State is not playing.
Waiting for key release prevents one long press from behaving like many separate presses.
Player sets Laser Active before broadcasting, so another loop pass cannot start a second shot.
Holding space sends many fire messages.
Place wait until not key space pressed or Game State is not playing inside the firing condition.
Set Laser Active to 1 before broadcasting.
Player stops moving while the Space key is held.
Keep movement and firing in two separate when I receive Start Game scripts.
Do not place the wait for the Space key release inside the movement loop.
Turn on the Laser Active variable display.
Click the green flag, then press and hold the Space key.
Laser Active changes from 0 to 1 once and stays 1, because the script that sets it back to 0 comes in the next step.
No clones are created.
Turn the display off again after the test.
Player contains no create clone block.
Player Laser contains no clone event.
The firing condition requires both space pressed and Laser Active equals 0.
When the Fire Laser message arrives, Player Laser moves to Player, starts a little above the ship, and travels upward.
The loop stops when the laser reaches the top, a collision sets Laser Active to 0, or play ends.
The same sprite then hides and becomes ready again.
On Player Laser, add a when I receive Fire Laser script.
The full script is in the finished code section on this page.
Add if Game State equals playing.
Inside it, use go to Player, then change y by 15.
That starts the shot 15 pixels higher, just above the ship.
Still inside the if block, show the sprite and add repeat until.
It stops when Laser Active equals 0, when y position is over 175, just below the top edge at y 180, or when Game State is not playing.
Inside the loop, change y by 10 and wait 0.02 seconds.
Each time the loop runs, the laser moves up 10 pixels.
Below the if block, not inside it, hide and set Laser Active back to 0.
These blocks run even when the game has ended, so the laser is always ready for the next shot.
Fire several separate shots.
Only one laser should be on the Stage at a time.
The repeat until condition uses one or operator inside another because any one of the three reasons should stop the laser.
Go to Player is safe here because Player is one sprite.
The later Enemy Shot will not go to an Alien.
The laser stays visible at the top.
Put hide after the repeat-until loop.
Check for y position greater than 175 in the loop condition.
Only the first shot works.
Set Laser Active to 0 after every flight ends.
Do not use stop this script before the cleanup blocks.
Fire one shot to the top, then fire again from a different Player position.
One visible laser rises from the current Player position, hides at the top, and can be reused.
Only one player laser can be visible.
The laser appears just above the ship, not on top of it.
Laser Active returns to 0 after each miss.
Each Alien clone checks whether the active Player Laser touches it.
The first clone hit sets Laser Active to 0 before changing the score and count.
Other clones then see that the hit was already handled, so the same laser cannot score twice.
Extend the Alien when I start as a clone script with a forever collision loop.
The full script is in the finished code section on this page.
Require Laser Active equals 1 and touching Player Laser in the same condition.
First set Laser Active to 0.
This tells the Player Laser to end its flight and hide, and tells other Alien clones that the hit was handled.
Add 10 to Score and subtract 1 from Aliens Left.
Delete this Alien clone last.
Shoot aliens in different rows and watch the visible Score and Aliens Left displays.
Blocks after delete this clone never run, so deletion must be last.
The original Alien never runs a clone-start script.
One laser destroys several aliens.
Set Laser Active to 0 before score, count, and deletion.
Confirm the laser is narrow enough that it does not begin inside two costumes.
The alien disappears but the count stays 24.
Change Aliens Left by -1 before deleting the clone.
Confirm you changed the Aliens Left variable made For all sprites, not a similarly named For this sprite only variable.
Destroy three aliens with three separate shots.
Score becomes 30, Aliens Left becomes 21, and exactly three aliens disappear.
Every hit adds exactly 10 points.
Every hit removes exactly one from Aliens Left.
A hit laser hides and becomes ready for another shot.
Fast shots can reveal blocks in the wrong order.
Test misses, hits, held keys, edge shots, and green-flag restarts now.
A short checklist is faster than guessing after you add more game systems.
Test a miss: move Player to the far left edge while the fleet is on the right side of the Stage, then fire.
The laser should reach the top without hitting anything and then hide.
Test a hit: fire at one alien.
Confirm that one alien disappears and Score goes up by 10.
Test a held key: hold the Space key while moving left and right.
Confirm that only one shot fires and that Player keeps moving.
Release the Space key and press it again to fire the next shot.
Test an edge position: move Player to each boundary and fire.
Test restart during flight: click the green flag while the laser is visible and confirm it hides and all 24 aliens return.
Fix each failed case before moving on.
Temporarily show Laser Active while debugging, then hide it.
A correct active value is always either 0 or 1.
A restart begins with fewer than 24 aliens.
The Stage must set Aliens Left to 0 before broadcast Reset Game and wait.
Do not broadcast Reset Game from any sprite or key.
The laser appears behind or inside Player.
